reviews.comment: Never posted notes, refused to review exam content before the exam, never clearly stated what material was going to be covered. Lectures were disorganized and rarely did examples in class. The homework was the only helpful portion of the class. The proofs on the exams were rarely encountered problems.

His lectures are boring and long and he speaks rather quietly. I sat in the first two rows and could barely understand what he was saying half the time. He seems very knowledgeable in mathematics but he really just isn't that great as a professor. Seemed like a nice guy and I wish I enjoyed his class more but it wasn't very interesting.

Little online material for this course besides the textbook. The professor does not use Canvas, so homework and grades are not posted. Assignments are given when a section is finished during lecture, its unpredictable when homework assigned and are due so basically lecture attendance is required. Important announcements are usually made in person.
if you have a sleep apnea he provides a great treatment... with the monotonous narrative of the book he will make you sleep in no time.

I don't see many reviews talking about this but you MUST go to class to know how well you're doing in the class. Nothing is online besides the homework and you will have to keep track of all the physical exams and quizzes returned to you to calculate your grade on your own.

He has super confusing lectures :( At this point I have only learned anything from the homework. Test reviews had no key so you have no idea if you're doing questions right or wrong. Reviews are true to the exam 50% of the time. Had a bad TA (which isn't entirely his fault) that only made my understanding worse. Take anyone else.
Good guy, everything is written on a whiteboard, absolutely nothing online.

Some reviews talk about Dykema having a lot of homework, but relative to other 221 professors (specifically Yaskin) he had much much less. Generally the lectures where all you needed to do well, those of us who regularly went did fine, but that was less than half the class after the first month. TL:DR if you care it's a pretty free A.
His lectures weren't my favorite. Half of the time I didn't know what he was talking about since he goes more in theory and abstract ways rather than doing examples.

Professor turned me away from the entire discipline of metric analysis with his hostile nature of pedagogy. His tests were unreasonably difficult and time restricted, and his methods of grading is questionable at best. His homeworks take hours with little rime or reason in terms of grading and feedback. The only non A I ever received in undergrad.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Retrospectively, KD was great. Very difficult topics, but lectures are clear. HW took incredibly long and I often needed to consult the internet/textbook. He's personable + friendly for help. Very fair tests (similar to old reviews, no surprises) Must attend class to succeed. Read chapter before starting each HW, start early! Do reviews to do well.

I got a bad grade but that was my fault. I think if you try hard enough he will help you out and help you get a decent grade. I would recommend going to class if you want a good grade, which I didn't do...

Before the final I had an 82 so I think he kept my B even after getting a C on all exams/final. I am pretty sure he gave me a B because I went to every class, asked questions, and even went to office hours. The topic itself is difficult but he gave leniency on exams. He is probably the best professor if this class is a requirement for you.

All I can tell you are facts. Started with 30+ students but by the ONE midterm for the whole class there were only 14 of us. Out of 14 straight A's, double major, and honors kids he failed 7. The curve extended a C to a 60, the only reason half of the class passed. If you don't write proofs EXACTLY like him you get a zero, even if you are right.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (Fall 22) Main problem with this professor is his style of teaching. It's not for everyone. He tends to focus more on the definition and "in theory" of concepts and doesn't really do any practice problems. For his exams, the questions were almost identical to the practice with different numbers. Recitation is mandatory because of a 2 question quiz.

I enjoyed his lectures, they were abstract, sure, but the homework was a good complement to them in applying the concepts we learned. Goofy guy, tests very similar to review questions so be sure to complete the reviews. Overall a very fair class, he was always willing to answer questions and is a good lecturer if you can handle abstract learning.

Dykema is very smart and definitely knows the topics he's teaching, but his way of teaching is very difficult to learn from. His teaching is primarily abstract, with little to no examples given. I would mostly learn from the textbook, homework, and the TA.

Dykema is a very intelligent person. But, his lectures are just pointless proofs/words that would fill a 20 ft whiteboard with almost no examples. Study the textbook religiously as his lectures render useless to his exams. He has strict grading, almost to the point of disbelief. Calc 3 is not impossible but he makes it close. Incredibly boring btw.
Awful. Grades incredibly harshly and nothing is clear. Very test heavy.

His lectures are boring and lack energy, and he grades tough. Why he's a 1 is because he was surprised that the averages on his first test were so low, and blamed either the pandemic or our "study habits", neither of which are why. Your test averages are so low because your lectures are terrible. The class itself isn't hard but I'd pass on Dykema.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To make this rate my professor review concise, I use another teachers website to study for his class. His lectures are all theoretical with little to no examples questions and the homework is only sometimes related to what he teaches to the point where I had to get outside help. I imagine some could learn from his class but it wasn't for me.

Dr. Dykema is a very nice person but is not a good lecturer. The lectures are purely conceptual and difficult to understand. Hardly any practice problems are done in class which does not help students for the exams or quizzes. The homework is optional but there are weekly quizzes. The majority of the grade comes from 3 exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a bit boring, but that's okay! He does a great job at teaching calculus. Stay on top of the weekly homework, and remember to attend recitation for quizzes. That's why I got a B. Great prof.

His class was very boring but he's a decent professor if you pay attention. Most of the learning happens through the webassign homework. Sometimes hard to follow but overall pretty decent professor. The first test was very easy but the second and the final were pretty hard. And he's a tough grader.

Honestly, he was a great professor for me. He can be a bit scatter brained sometime but that's perfectly fine if you go back and read over your notes and do a lot of problems besides the homework. I studied a lot and I still got a B, but to me I earned that B. That being said I would still take him again. :))
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty boring, but some people are able to understand what is going on. Most of the learning comes from webassign problems. Quizzes reflect the homework. Exams, except exam 1 are difficult. Exam 1 is just like the study guide he gives but the other exams are much more difficult. Beware of quizzes every Friday.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If there exists a archetypal mathematician, then Dykema is it. This isn't at all a bad thing: he cares about the details, gives the theory behind concepts in lecture, and expects you to generally do things in a mathematically sound manner. Homework, quizzes, and tests were all fair and covered what you'd expect if you went to lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He tends to mumble towards the board, so it's hard to understand him. He doesn't post grades anywhere, so you have to keep track yourself. There are weekly quizzes to make sure you're actually studying, but they generally come after the homework. He doesn't require a textbook, but some things may be easier to learn from it rather than from him.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures can be all over the place at times and hard to follow. The material is pretty difficult at times to grasp at first, but there is a lot of HW so you can be prepared. The quizzes were very similar to exam problems. He gives out an exam review but without answers. Open to questions though. He is nice, grades fairly, and overall good prof
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'd get lost in lecture sometimes but mostly due to the difficulty of the material, rather than poor instruction. Weekly WebAssign HW and quizzes. If you don't understand something in class, the HW is useful in learning it. Dykema is a fair prof. Gives out an exam review (no answers, but very open to questions during office hours).
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Woud recommend this professor. The syllabus is very clear and the workload is manageable. He gives an exam review that is a very good gauge of how the exam will be like. I recommend you know that exam review very well. Very nice and helpful when you ask him questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher. Very scatterbrained and is all over the place. Hard to learn from

This teacher is very insightful and you learn a lot in the class, don't listen the comment right under mine, his probably a freshman who does nothing and just came from high school. I took Calc 3 and I have learned alot in math and I am a freshman who actually knows what his doing.
I actually failed his class and had to retake it. His tests weren't that hard but his final was. HE DOESN"T CURVE. STUDY HARD especially for the 3rd and final tests.
